transcript: Interview Guide. Activity E. FGD:  Aspirations of Youth
Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)
The result of private voting

Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 0 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 1 vote; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 5 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 2 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 1 vote; total: 9 votes

The literacy rate is still low in our village. At present, boys are studying for their career development and trying to get good job those already fished their study. They are working hard and trying to improve their social position.

Most people of our village engaged in agricultural activities so their economic power is limited. They can’t make all important life decision. At present, they can make decision in certain aspects but not all as they have limited power.

Majority of the people here are lower middle and middle class farmer. They have little skill in modern agricultural activities. In the past, many of the village inhabitants worked as day laborer but this number has reduced now. And these people are moving to agricultural activities and improving their economic conditions. Currently, many become solvent.

Most of the farmers cannot buy and apply appropriate amount of fertilizer in their cultivable lands although they have wish to buy but they don’t have enough money. These people work hard and try to enhance their economic position.

These people can have three meals but they cannot take all major life decisions but in some respect they do. They cannot support their children’s higher education. Their income is limited and they always struggle to live with their limited income.

In the past, over 90 percent people could not support their children’s education. But now this situation almost reversed. Local farmers are adopting new agricultural technologies and gaining from these practices. Many people sent their children abroad and built new house. Thus, local peoples’ decision making capacity has been increasing day by day here.
Youths are depended on their parental decision. They receive monetary support from their parents in every respect. So, they can take limited decisions without parents/father’s permission.

All the FGD participants showed their interest in education. They think education /schooling is very important. They mention, “Education is fundamental right of all human”. Besides, illiterate people cannot make right decision in many issues. Without education there is possibility to make faults in decision.

We think we can have better livelihood opportunities if we have higher education. Some youths obtain it but many cannot obtain. To read and write is fundamental requirement for many purposes. Education is essential someone moves to city or a foreign country. They cannot find a right direction if they don’t have minimum education.

I think education can help in many aspects. Education is essential for better agricultural farming. An educated farmer can change his economic position quickly. One can move or take decision more confidently if s/he is educated. Life is not easy with education. It is not possible to get a respectable job in job market without an education or running a business.
Schooling is necessary for obtaining knowledge and skills. Education helps ones overall welfare.

At present in our village, 80-85 percent boys complete their Junior School Certificate (JSC) and among these boys 50 percent try to complete up to secondary school certificate (SSC) level. About 30 percent complete Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and only 5-10 percent go for Bachelors and to universities for higher education.

And most girls in this village go up to eight to nine grades. Then their parents become worried for their marriage. A few of the married girls continue their education even after their marriage. About 40 percent girls obtained their SSC and 20-25 percent HSC and only 5 percent girls go for Bachelor Degrees.

But most girls can complete up to eight grades and at this level their parents arrange marriage. Most girls cannot study because of their early marriage. A few girls from well of households get opportunity for better education and can go for professional career.

I think all boys should complete at least HSC (higher secondary certificate) and if possible go for higher education and the girls should complete at least SSC. Boys and girls should obtain same level of knowledge. Girls could be free from superstition and good teacher to their children if they complete at least SSC.
Sustaining is very difficult without education in present era.

I think all boys and girls should have at least SSC. And higher education (Honors and Masters Degrees) is necessary if someone wants a decent job. But all youths cannot get opportunity for higher education for economic insolvency, this is the reality here.
Early marriage could be prevented if girls get more opportunity to complete up to intermediate level. In the future, without a SSC no one can get adjust with others in the society.
Parents do not show same commitment to educating their daughters as their sons in our village.
In our village, the parents have different promise and commitment for sons and daughters’ education. [all participants are agreed].
Agriculture depended households

Most parents do not take same commitment for educating their sons and daughters in our village. Because they think the investment on daughters’ education could not benefitted the parents but investment on son’s education must return with additional benefits.

I think most parents take same commitment for their daughters’ until their marriage. But they arranged their marriage as early as possible and after that they don’t think about their daughters’ interest. They think their daughter could not support them after marriage.
I think our parents should give same importance and priority for both sons and daughters. But this is not reality here because the parents do not offer same opportunity for their sons and daughters.
My opinion is in our village, boys assist their fathers in agricultural activities. But girls cannot do that. Moreover, parents cannot commit same promise due to their inadequate financial capacity.
I think most poor parents ignore their daughters and realize that educating their daughters is not essential. For this reason, they do not show same commitment to them.

In our village, most boys start assisting their fathers and elder brothers as early as 9-10 years. They assist their father’s agricultural works and look domestic animals. At this level, they learn to weeds in their fields and also keep cattle and collect grasses for domestic animals.

I started [one participant] agricultural works when I was 10 years old. Many boys of our village start works when they just 9-10 years old. At this level, they collect animals’ fodders, take care of them etc. They learn small works in agricultural farming e.g. weeding, seed planting, harvesting etc.
And at 11-12 years, many boys learn to assist sowing, rice, wheat, maize and other crops, harvest and also learn transplantation, weeding ploughing, irrigating with their father and elder brothers.
After 15 most boys become household countable man power because they already learnt most part of agricultural activities.
On the other hand, 9-10 years, girls learn household chores and assist their mothers. They can look after goats and chickens and assists their mothers in the kitchen garden and household’s work.
Reasons for ending education
Among various reasons, many boys stopped their schooling due to inadequate financial capacity. There is no available money at hand to support. So, the poverty sill is a factor for rural households.
Secondly: I think lack of awareness of parents is second important reason for ending their children’s education.
Many parents engaged their children in work early. Such children could attend school regularly. In some point, they lose their motivation for school education.
Some boys stopped education here because they are lazy. A few surely stopped education after an affair with a girl and do not concentrate in education.
A few boys stopped because they become addicted to harmful elements.
Some boys also stopped while they spoil time and money and spend it to girls and other likeminded friends. Parents try to control their sons but when they failed to do so then, they stop paying.
Some boys also ended their education when their parents arrange early marriage.
Some parents are not aware and do not understand the value of education. They put pressure on their children for work. So, the children cannot attend their class regularly.
Most parents arranged their daughters’ marriages as early as possible. As a result, so many girls either dropped out or stopped their schooling.
Some children stopped education when their main earning person/father died or when parents marriage breakdown.
All participants put the reasons below accordingly:

Prime Cause -1: The most important reason for quit schooling is poverty or household income is still limited. The poverty has been killing peoples’ dream of education. In our village many boys had to stop their schooling due to their economic insolvency. In such condition, parents engage their children to work. These children become lost their attention in education.

Cause 2: Then all participants put the most important 2nd cause is arranging early marriage for daughters and sons as well and engaging in work. Early marriage hampers both the boys and girls educational life. They have to start household works or earn an income after marriage. Many boys stopped their education when their parents engage them in work early.
I wish I could have completed my education and start a professional career. But that was possible for me.
I am studying because my goal is after complete my study I want to be economically solvent as well as a wise person in our village. I wanted to be respected by surrounded society.
I am studying because I wanted to be a respected person and establish my head high here.
I could not continue my schooling because of financial crisis in the family.
Another participant said, I want to complete my higher education first then I want to construct a livestock farm here. This is my aim.
Educated person has special position in the society. People respect them. Education makes efficient in communications.
Most youths entered to agricultural work and other petty trades or search a job when they are no longer students. Some youths migrate to XX city or a foreign country.

Again, some youths try to get private professional jobs those have obtained bachelor or masters degrees. Many youths get self employed and drive autos, easy bike and Nochhimon or rickshaw/van nowadays.
Some also sell their labor during pick season when they are no longer a student. Again, when there is no local agricultural work available some youths start small shops.
Some youths start medium size business particularly those parents have a good bank balance.

One participant said, I think young men should start an income earning job/activities or at least engage in agricultural work when they stopped their schooling. They should spend time without doing anything. What they get they should start one, for example, agricultural activities, driving, petty trade, or day laborer etc.
They can find a small job with private companies or NGOs if he completed SSC. They can have experience if start one such job. He should have skills for specific goal.

I think educated men should do job or until get they should look for a good job. And if they have secondary or higher secondary education they can enter job in RMG sector or other industrial job. They can do private tuition.
On the other hand, those who have financial capability they may start a business otherwise can enter in agricultural practices.

Now we are producing many diversified crops those including wheat (Prodeep, Bijoy Shotabdi and seeds from neighboring Indian farmers), rice, lentil, jute, potato, mustard seed, and various fruits. And so many vegetables are also included. Improved seed varieties and seedlings are coming in our area. Actually, many new agricultural elements have been included in agricultural practices within the last five years or so.

CIMMYT partner JCF introduced new agricultural technologies also added in agricultural farming e.g. seeder machine (PTOS) machine and some other machines e.g. thresher, motorized irrigation pump, fertilizers and pesticides. Bed planter system not introduced yet in our village.
New ideas, knowledge, trainings, and agriculture field school, demonstration plots etc. are also introduced here.

Jagorani Chakra Foundation (JCF), IMPACT, Bangladesh Agriculture Extension department and have been working with the farmers. These organizations are also playing very important roles in agricultural advancement. XX and XX are also providing new knowledge on fertilizers, pesticides and improved seed varieties.
We think for male farmers, the improved seed varieties are most important here. [All FGD participants are agreed].

They put improved seeds as Rank 1 item because the farmers are enhancing their well-being through modern agricultural practices where improved seeds are most important item for getting better production.

All participants (9) are agreed, what way to cultivate with new seeds? Trainings and knowledge regarding modern agricultural practices are also very important for farmers. Training can provide a right way to do the farming. This is also making farmers efficient and confident.

The participants also think that the improved agricultural trainings as Rank 2. Because without this new training production cannot be increased and costs of agricultural practices cannot feasible or competitive. The agricultural production has been increasing due to improved trainings.

For women famers, number one item is improved seed varieties. Improved seed is important for all farmers. And the second most important item is improved agricultural technologies. So, the second important item for women is improved agricultural technologies. Besides, women farmers should have training regarding seed preserving.

The female youths do not have same opportunity on agricultural trainings whether it is wheat or rice related training. The local norms and customs do not permit women’s independent participation as like as men.

In our village, some women get chance to participate in Math Dibosh where participants get important information and consultations from agricultural experts. But these women cannot experiment themselves in the fields.
This type of program can encourage women to participate and obtain new cultivation techniques.

My opinion is that there is very limited scope for women attending in the government agricultural training programs. In our area, there is no social restriction for women’s participation but social norms are still rigid for women’s economic activities.
Module 2.  Gender norms, livelihoods, and family formation (1 ½ hours)

Important wheat innovation for men Ten years ago
• Most farmers used local and traditional wheat seeds. The yield was very poor. No improved wheat seeds introduced like today..
• Farmers used only Sonali, Kanchon and some other local varieties;
• Farmers used local and traditional farming methods. No new technologies like Strip Tillage.
• Inadequate knowledge on raising livestock and chicken
• Knowledge and information sharing were not prominent 10 years ago.
There were no improved seeds ten years ago here. Most farmers prepare and preserve seeds for own use and sell excess seeds.
Most farmers follow the conventional system in wheat cultivation which requires more time, labor and money. But the yield was less compared to present time.

Most women in the farmers’ households have conventional knowledge on seeds preservation. They never depend on market seeds. But the yield was poor compare to current productivity. In production, rice, wheat, maize, lentil and mustard are much ahead of others. In the past, a few large landholding farmers could have sold their access products. But today many subsistence farmers sell their additional products.

Most farmers plough their lands by bullock and buffalo but now it is done by power tiller/tractor. Besides other new technologies, e.g. PTOS machine is reducing the cost and time in agricultural farming. The seeder method has reduced quantity of irrigation in the wheat/maize cultivation. The man power necessity also reduced in the bed planter or in the strip tillage methods. Rat attack has reduced the wastes.
Bullock plough was the main methods for land tilling and no power thresher introduced in our village. This crop threshing has saved a lot of labors.

Yes, there are social norms and religious interpretations which regulate the various works and gender responsibilities in the agricultural activities. The local youths are following the tradition. Young men can do all sort of works in crop cultivation.

On the other hand, women have to start some household works e.g. cleaning house premises, wash all utensils, clean the cowshed and cook foods and serve to all family members. These are all done by women. No men or boys are not familiar or habituate to do these works. These are treated as feminine works.

Again, collecting fodder for cows, preparing lands, transplanting, weeding, sowing, harvesting etc. is men’s work. And carrying loads from field, selling agricultural products in market are also men’s work.
Caring and raising chickens, duck and cultivating vegetables in the kitchen garden are task of woman.

For social reasons, women cannot participate in practical agricultural activities. They are not allowed to carry loads from the field. It is assumed that women’s body is soft and less sturdy to do hard work like men.
But women practically work and assist husband in the crop fields nowadays but it was not possible before.

In our village, no women are allowed to harvest wheat and rice. This is men’s job and their domain where women cannot go and participate. Similarly women will be highly discouraged to sell wheat or rice in our local market.

Local women feel ashamed in the field and market. Very poor women can move to these works if she is widow, or she has no father, brother or grown-up son. But for a young woman there will be problem and social restriction.
Some women work in the field sometimes but this is not a regular practice in our village. Sometimes they assist to their husbands in harvesting or other works but this is not open accepted practice.
One exceptional is accepted as the young women can participate jointly with men in field training sessions.

Producing and selling of agricultural products is generally accepted and also appreciated when a young man grows wheat, maize, rice and or vegetables in his fields. This has been going on for years. The farmers and neighbors will encourage those youths.
Our society (samaj) accepts youth can grow and sell any products whether it is agricultural products or animals. But many young men are reluctant working in the fields.
Social restrictions are for women not for men. So, men can grow and sell any products in nearby or distant market there is no prohibition for his activities.

Cultivating a specific crop depends according to various facilities are available on and roadside land or soil quality. Low land is not appropriate for wheat or maize cultivation but could be good for hybrid rice. Crop cultivation can be changed when surrounding farmers shifting one crop type to another. However, selection of crop and land is the responsibility of men.

This is always decided by father or who manages the crops cultivation. There is no separate decision maker for men’s and women’s land in one household. Land may be entitled by both husband and wife but all lands are supervised by father/husband.
Again, older son make decision but consulting with mother if father died or absent.
In our village, women entitled little amount of cultivable land and men doesn’t want that. Women do not look after or selection of crop.
In our village and surrounding areas, there is no such norm here. Most plots are cultivated and supervised by men or husband or grow-up sons whether those plots are owned by men or women.
In husband’s absence, women can look after crops and make major decisions herself. She may consult with other family members or good farmers in the village.

There is no common practice of working jointly in crop plots in our village. But only the poor women work in the crop field with her husband or women help their husbands during the harvesting time when shortage of labour.

There are no social restrictions or rules for men to work women’s lands. In all cultivable lands of a household, male members work and manage. Family members do not separate work as per land ownership.
Similarly, women work their husbands’ lands but cannot make major decision. It is mentionable that almost all the cultivable lands and homesteads are entitled to men in our village.
Women and men as well consult with other skilled farmers when start a new crop.
Woman also talks to her grown-up son and her husband if he is still alive. And if her husband died then she consults with her in-laws, and other neighbours and local good farmers.
On the other hand, a good husband consults with his wife when he is going to plant a new crop or use a new technology.
Usually a man consults with good and skilled farmers and sometimes with local seed dealers.
Most youth participants think, men give little importance to their wives opinion.
[All participants heard the Adam and Ana’s story attentively]

All FGD participants (9) agreed that Adam will accept Ana’s joining a local women’s group. There is no contradiction in her joining because she is a vegetable grower like other women and she wants to develop her production. But there could barriers if the trainer is a man.

The participants think this joining is positive for their household. She may get new ideas or training which will enrich vegetable cultivation and income. This is the main reason for allowing her to join.
[All the participants raised their hands and show their consent]
All participants (9) express their disagreement:
Adam will not accept Ana’s decision regarding selling vegetable in the local market herself.
Adam will tell Ana that he will go to market for selling her vegetables but he will not allow her going to market for selling vegetable.
He will not accept her assistance in crop fields.
[All 9 participants raised their hands and show their consent]
My opinion, Adam would not accept Ana’s help in his crop fields. Crop fields are public place.
Another participant said, “I will never take her with me in field. I would like her to work at home”.
In anyway, Adam would not allow her to go to field for work.
[All 9 participants raised their hands and show their consent]
In our village, there will be no social dignity if Mary herself sells her vegetables in the local market.
Mary has inferior social position and dignity in the village because she sells her vegetables whiles her husband alive. She will lose her respect (tar somman thakbe na) and reputation.
Most people see her badly since she is going to market place. Other men will laugh at her and make jokes about her.
Some may buy her products but would not give the price to her. She has no dignity as she is not obeying the social regulations.
Nine participants are agreed.
Mark has no social status and dignity in the village. Many people would ridicules Mark. Most people especially his friends will make jokes about him and his reputation will be in stake.

Mark’s friends may not say bad comments in front of him but behind him they will do so. He must lose his respects (somman harabe) from others. Some may ask him what type of husband you are. Some may say him, “why your wife is going to marker when you are here?” Some friends may go beyond!!
[All the participants expressed their consent]
Mark will be delighted and happy as she is successful in her initiative.
Mark will be happy as he observing their economic advancement.
[Nine participants are agreed]

Equality means equal rights. There is no practice of equality in our village. Because women have to work in the domain of household and men work in the crops fields. Men are also work in the market where they accomplish their tasks. I think this is equality here.

This is also equality when a sister gets half portion of land of their brother because Islam prescribed this for Muslim people. Boys assist their parents for income earning activities much before than their sisters. Father buys land with those incomes. This is another reasons that brother should gets double of their sister.
There is no equality here. This is not good. I think people moves forward and advance economically in the household when there is equality.

I think equality is an understanding between couples or men and women. A household cannot progress if there is no such condition. There will be no equality if I don’t give importance to my wife’s word or talk with angrily. When a husband gives rights to his wife and his wife does the same that is equality.

Equality is good in some extent but not at all respects. Equality is surely good if parents take same commitment for their both sons and daughters. But it is not right to allow her to go to the local market.
I think Diana will take this decision because she knows how much to keep for own consumption and how much to sell. [All 9 participants agreed]
I think David cannot make this decision because he does not know their own household’s necessity. [All 9 participants agreed]
Of course, David must be sold the vegetables not possible for Diana.
[All 9 participants agreed]
Men should sell their vegetables this normal activity for men here. This is consistent social norm for men here because women are ignorant about the right prices of particular vegetables.

David is a man and this is his responsibility. Man can go to market by any local vehicle but that is not possible for Diana. Moreover, David never allows her wife to go to market because market is not women’s place.
[All 9 participants are agreed]
Surely, David will pay attention to Diana’s proposal and requirements of the cultivation.
There will be no problems because the prospect is good. So, David accepts her plan and they will try it for additional income. There will be no problem.
[All 9 participants are agreed]
When Diana receives inheritance from her natal family and goes ahead for purchasing a plot. The participants expressed their responses as:

How easy or difficult for Diana to purchase the plot of land without David’s support (private rating): 1 = Very easy: 3 votes; 2 = Easy: 1 vote; 3 = Neither easy nor difficult: 3 votes; 4 = Difficult: 2 votes; 5 = Very difficult: 0 votes; total: 9 votes
I think this would easy for Diana because she is going to get the inheritance. She has money at her hand. So, she will buy the plot although her husband is not agreed.
This would be easy for her because she is going buy a land. The society around will support Diana not to David.

It will be quite difficult for Diana because her husband wants to buy a motorbike with her inheritance money. He will be furious and mad if he cannot establish his plan. She is not obeying her husband which makes her plan difficult.
A woman cannot establish her plan without her husband’s permission. If Diana goes ahead with her plan alone there will be huge clash and violence between husband and wife.

There is a chance to breakdown their marriage. David may divorce her if she does not accept his plan. David thinks his wife should handover the money to him. And he can buy the motorbike with that money. Other there will be bad consequence to her fate. That is Divorce.
There will be huge clash and quarrel between David and Diana if she goes ahead without gives David much attention and consultation.
When David receives inheritance from his natal family and goes ahead for purchasing a motorbike. The participants expressed their responses as:

How easy or difficult for David to purchase the motorbike without Diana’s support (private rating): 1 = Very easy: 8 votes; 2 = Easy: 1 vote; 3 = Neither easy nor difficult: 0 votes; 4 = Difficult: 0 votes; 5 = Very difficult: 0 votes; total: 9 votes
For David this will be relatively easier to establish his plan because the money is coming from his family. So, it is his money. He can use that money for his pleasure.
One participant said, “This is very easy for David” [all participants laugh].
David is a man and he must have hobby desire for motorbike. Now he has money and demand. He will buy a motorbike.
At day time, any young and adult women can walk to the local market or a public place alone here.
This can be difficult for them after sun set. The family will not allow them to move at that time.

After marriage, there is no big changed here for young women’s movement to local public place or a market. They get permission from her parents before marriage and she take from her husband after marriage.
In social custom here that young women don’t move to the local market after marriage. If urgent then she takes someone with her.
A young woman is supervised by natal families before her marriage and those responsibilities shifted to husband and his family after marriage.

Local women never go to the local for sell their products here. The social regulation and practice do not allow women to move to market for selling products. She loses her social dignity and reputation of the family.
This is impossible for her. This will spoil her seclusion (porda noshto hobe). She cannot maintain her porda when she sells her products in the market.
Private Vote for Rating of women’s Movement

Out of every 10 women, how many move freely on their own in public spaces (private rating): 1 (practically no women move freely on their own in the village): 0 votes; 2: 2 votes; 3: 1 vote; 4: 0 votes; 5: 0 votes; 6: 0 votes; 7: 0 votes; 8: 0 votes; 9: 0 votes; 10 (practically all women move freely on their own in the village): 6 votes (9)
At day time, most women can move freely here;
Young women alone can move to their school and college here and also to the local market for buying their necessity.
Family does allow their daughter’s movement alone. There are no social and religious restrictions in our area women’s movement
It would be difficult for a youth with a proper channel or a connection.
It would be easier if he has a good close friends or relatives in that city. Without these facilities that would be quite difficult for him to obtain a job there.
To get a job could be easier if he has some education, experience and good manner.
Get a job immediately is possible for a fresh youth without having connection with friends or relatives. Sustaining would be difficult for him in the new place.
Many youths and young women have migrated to XX from our village and a few also migrated abroad. These people are actually contributing a lot and changing their households’ situation.
A few friends could be happy but most of friends do not take him back easily. Some friends may make joke and laugh at him. For family, it would be shocking.
Local people say that he is not active in work but a work cheater. That is why he returned back to village.

Some people or relative may say that he has no patience in his job. Many people do not take him easily and some will make fun of his return. A local youth got a job with national force but he returned. His parents never take him easy or he could not recover his position in his family since then. His friends also did not like his return.
He has rights to start local works e.g. engaged in farming, or sells labour or start a small business and can drive autos.
Some cannot adjust with local work then they move idly here and there. They are not accepted cordially by parents, friends and neighbours.
Most formal marriages are arranged by families and relatives for males and females here;

In our area, most male youths get married when they become 18 to 20 years. And about 80-85 percent families arranged their daughter’s marriage within the age of 14-15 years. Some parents also arrange their daughters’ before 14n years. This is not high number.
About 5-10 percent girls got married consensually and rest of the 10 percent get married when they become 16 and above.
A few girls get married late. They try to complete their education and then go for marriage.

About 90 percent marriage decisions are taken by parents and elderly people in our village. And 8-10 percent marriages are ‘love marriages’. These boys and girls love each other and ran away for getting marriage. Many parents do not recognize such marriages or take time for parental acceptance.
In our village, some boys oppose their parental decision on age of marriage and bride sometimes. But daughters must accept and obey her parents’ decisions regarding their marriage.
I think decision about marriage should be taken by parents and the family because they understand this matter better than me. We should marry someone according to parents’ decision.
Parents should sit with son/daughter before finalizing a marriage decision.
I think parents should not take marriage decision alone. They should allow their children to choose and making this vital decision.
Marriage decision should be taken by all family members jointly and there should be consultation with boys and girls.
In our village, about most married women get first baby after 1-2 years of their marriage.
Most of the marriage women get first child when they reach about 16 to 17 years.
A few married women take first child when they become 18 years and above.
Sixteen or seventeen years are not appropriate time for become a new mother because she does not know how to take care of own health and her baby at this stage.
In our village, some married young women take first baby when they themselves are children. Many maternal deaths are still occurring for this reason.
Many girls also suffer with anaemia and lack of nutrition.
I think women should not have first child before 18 years and the new couple should take first baby when they become 22-23 years. This is suitable time for having baby.
Most youth participants said,
Women should have baby during their twenties. Having a first baby before this age is not good for their physical and mental health.
Some youths also said, at 20-22 years is most perfect age for having first baby because these at this stage woman get ready mentally and physically and they can take proper care.
One youth said, a new wife cannot this decision herself or she does not have rights to make this decision.

Another married youth said, I make this decision after consulting with my wife. Both husband and wife jointly take this important decision in this village. This decision should not be taken alone whether this is by wife or husband.
But there are social pressures from elderly family members to have baby as early as well.
At present, many couples use contraceptives which reduce the number children and gaps between two children;
We want to see all our youths are educated here in the future.
We want see that all early marriages stopped here and the multiple marriages practice (only a few) has stopped as well.
We strongly expect that no women are taking first baby early anymore in the future. The awareness programs worked really well in this purpose.
We want to see our village a develop clean and beautiful one in the future;
We also want to see our farmers are using most modern equipments and technologies in our agricultural practices.
The parents are supporting their daughters and sons’ education equally and taking same commitment for them.
We want to see our village where nobody is addicted to any harmful materials. And wish to see this no girls are facing eve teasing or any harassment.
No one should be deprived of education here.
I want to see my village a modern and ideal one.
We also expect that we could work and make contribution for our country;
